decisions.reason: As a recent launch close to the core enterprise communications offer, management is likely to continue backing it and explain weak traction as temporary while trying to leverage existing customer relationships.
It fits the firm's owned metro, data centre and cloud connectivity strengths and already shows visible market adoption, so both strategic commitment and early validation argue strongly for retention.

This service builds directly on the firm's fibre and high-bandwidth infrastructure and was given a dedicated webpage, indicating a public commitment that management will be reluctant to reverse quickly.
A voice number ordering portal supports the stated move toward software-defined and real-time provisioning, so recent investment and strategic fit make continuation more likely than withdrawal.

Carrier pre-selection looks like a more legacy telephony product with weak fit to the announced direction toward smarter integrated infrastructure services, so it is the easiest offer to sacrifice despite some sunk-cost pressure to persist.

A direct voice network connection service remains close to the firm's established voice and network business, so management would usually keep it on the market at least another year while hoping enterprise demand stabilises.
